incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED: policy-engine runtime panic on router-prod-3 (smart-routing) — severity=high, impact=customer-facing
incident-bot: root_ts=1854321987 — auto-created incident channel

michelle.eng: looking into it now. logs show a panic during rule evaluation in the fallback policy. stack (trimmed):
```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
goroutine 274 [running]:
github.com/redwood/policy/engine.(*Evaluator).Eval(0xc0004b8000, 0xc000a1f000, 0x40)
	/var/lib/jenkins/workspace/policy/engine/eval.go:162 +0x1f3
main.handleRequest(0xc0009a4000)
	/opt/service/router/main.go:88 +0x45
```

sam.oncall: paging @_oncall_team — taking pager. which policy rule hit?

michelle.eng: initial parse points to `route_variant_by_customer`. looks like a mapping helper returned an empty string which then flowed into an expression that expects a non-empty variant and caused a nil-deref. snippet that failed:  
```
when request.region =~ /eu/ && model.variant == "auto"
  -> variant = pick_variant(customer, "recommended")
```
`pick_variant` resolved to an empty name for some customers because the mapping referenced `gpt-open-7b-q4_cpu`, which isn't present in GPU pools' catalog. downstream code assumed variant != "".

alex.platform: fyi we recently rolled a mapping that adds cpu-only fallback names for some open models. if smart-routing tries to pick that for a GPU-backed route it trips later checks and creates a fallback loop.

carla.sre: customer impact: 502/503 spikes and higher tail latency across multiple routes (/v1/chat, /v1/complete, /v1/embeds). error-rate peaked ~28% us-east-1, ~12% eu-west-1. SLO pages triggered.

lina-cs: CS note — two enterprise customers (acme-inc, finlytics) opened support tickets for job timeouts. both use Dedicated but rely on smart-routing for cross-region failover.

sam.oncall: immediate mitigations I'm applying now:
- flip feature flag to disable smart-routing on prod-router clusters (route.context.smart_routing = false)
- pin model.variant for affected endpoints to `gpt-redwood-7b-v1`
- temporarily increase fallback pool capacity in eu-west
I'll run the control-plane commands and report back.

michelle.eng: quick config note — policy-engine has `panic_on_missing_variant` true in prod. if we set it false, evaluator will return a default route instead of panicking. could avoid the crash while we fix mapping.

alex.platform: running commands now:
```
redwoodctl config set /services/router-prod/policy-engine/panic_on_missing_variant false --env=prod
redwoodctl route update --selector=path:/v1/* --set model.variant=gpt-redwood-7b-v1 --env=prod
```

sam.oncall: applied both. disabling smart-routing flag next.
sam.oncall: `redwoodctl feature-flag set smart-routing false --env=prod`

incident-bot: action recorded by sam.oncall: smart-routing=disabled at 1854322005

carla.sre: seeing errors drop on eu-west, traffic stabilizing. still processing some backlog from requests that hit the loop earlier. tailing logs now.

michelle.eng: root-cause analysis in progress — policy helpers allowed empty variant names to propagate. adding guard in `pick_variant` and a unit test for empty/unknown keys. preparing a hotfix branch.

michelle.eng: opened hotfix PR: https://git.redwood/eng/policy-engine/pulls/428 — adds `if variant == "" { return default_variant }` plus regression tests and an integration case for GPU pool compatibility.
